Design Palette

Design Book

1,220 sq ft · 2 bed / 3 bath

A black-and-white checkerboard floor, set on the diagonal, runs through the entire home — bedrooms, living room, kitchen, dining room, entryways, closets — at one consistent size throughout, stopping at the stairs (reclaimed wood treads) and all three bathrooms, which take a small-format charcoal mosaic floor instead, paired with blue-green tiled walls and matte black hardware. The primary bedroom gets a pair of twin beds, plus a power recline love seat. The secondary bedroom gets full bed. The downstairs powder room is converted into a full bath laid out as a two-section curbless wet room, and the living room gets a matching power recline sofa.

A note on flexibility. The one must-have is the checkerboard tile throughout. Everything else — colors, materials, fixtures, and how to get the best value — is genuinely open to the design firm's judgment. This palette is a starting reference, not a locked spec. The general aesthetic direction we're after: fresh and current, the kind of space that photographs well today, but grounded enough in timeless choices that it won't read as dated in five or ten years.
By Room Material callouts and specifications
Primary Bedroom

Two separate twin beds give the kids who sleep here their own space. A power recline sleeper love seat sits between them for guests. The 13-foot wall behind both headboards and the sofa is wrapped floor to ceiling in the same wood-look plank tile used on the entryway wall, run vertically in 13 columns to pull the eye up — a durable, wipeable surface right where beds and furniture make contact. Checkerboard floor, gray walls in glossy finish elsewhere in the room. Closets stay open — doors come off, frames stay in place — fitted with built-in organizers and a built-in desktop. All hardware in matte black.

Primary Bathroom

Alcove tub / tile shower with matte black drain kit, right drain, and a curved shower curtain rod. Sea-glass ceramic in a wavy glossy glaze — set in a straight 6" grid — wraps the tub surround and carries straight on down the whole wall that holds the vanity and toilet, floor to ceiling — one continuous plane rather than a patch behind the mirror. Single 36" vanity, Acorn finish, black hardware provides unobstructed width to the tub's full alcove opening. Small-format charcoal mosaic floor, matching downstairs and the secondary bath, gray walls, matte black faucet, medicine cabinet, toilet, shower head + handheld wand for tub use.

Secondary Bedroom

Secondary Bathroom

Shower-only, no tub — the whole room takes the same small-format charcoal mosaic floor as downstairs and the primary bath, with a linear drain in the shower matching downstairs. Paired with the same blue-green glossy ceramic on the walls, set in the same straight 6" grid, wrapping the shower and continuing along the full wall that holds the vanity and toilet, floor to ceiling. A frameless sliding glass door, matte black, closes the full 60" opening. Single 30" vanity, Acorn finish, black hardware. Gray walls, matte black faucet, medicine cabinet, toilet, and a fixed shower head — no handheld wand.

Dining Room

Checkerboard floors, gray walls in glossy finish. Kitchen cabinets and counters extend across the length of the dining room with 36" counter depth to allow use as desk space at bar stool height and space to put a coffee machine. Dining table is 36" round dining table (white marble top, matte black base), paired with 4 black ash dining chairs. The existing slider is replaced with a matte black aluminum bi-fold door — three panels that fold away to open the wall to the patio.

Downstairs Bathroom

Powder room converted to a full bath: a curbless wet room split evenly into two 30.5" sections — shower to the west, toilet kept dry behind fixed glass to the east. Opal color tile runs floor-to-ceiling on three walls; only the pocket-door wall stays paint. A ceiling-mount rain head (no handheld wand — rain heads throw the least spray), the corner sink with a matte black single hole faucet and mirror above, the same Kingston toilet as elsewhere, and a 28" satin black pocket door. A rigid support bar from the west wall braces the glass panel and doubles as the curtain rod — the curtain screens the sink and walk-in from spray when drawn.

Proposed floor plan to fit a 3/4 bath in place of the existing 1/2 bath. 30.5" x 61" = 1861 sq in

Entryway

An archway passageway wall between the living room and kitchen. A tiled accent wall — wood-look ribbed ceramic in a plank format — wraps up and over the small ceiling section above it, reading as one clean, continuous statement; the long run of wall is exactly what the plank proportion and relief texture need to shine. Optional: a shoe storage bench along the wall. Checkerboard floors, gray walls elsewhere in the room.

Stairs

Connecting space between the living room and bedrooms upstairs. Reclaimed hardwood treads, milled with a built-up roundover nose, stained to the walnut tone used by the bedroom furniture and finished in a hard multi-coat clear, over white-painted risers. Walls confirmed gray, glossy finish. All railings and hardware in matte black.

Appendix Bathroom wall tile options
Whole House Tile Options

The two tiles used across the whole house, outside the bathrooms: Leona for the checkerboard floor, Zayne for the accent walls (both bedrooms plus the entry). Neither had a serious rival considered — this page documents them the same way the bathroom wall tile page documents its five, for reference.

12" x 12" checkerboard set · matte porcelain, marble-look
SPECIFIED
Reflectance · 16% (black) / 85% (white)
Price$9.25 / sq ft
Box$278.29 / 30.08 sf set (32 pc, 2 boxes: 1 black + 1 white)
LayoutWhole house, set on the diagonal, one size throughout

Set on the diagonal, one consistent 12" size throughout the home — bedrooms, living room, kitchen, dining room, entryways, closets — stopping at the stairs and all three bathrooms. Both squares read warm despite reading as neutral marble.

Zayne Slat
nominal 12" x 36" (actual 11.81" x 35.43") · matte ceramic, fluted
SPECIFIED
Reflectance · 56.2%
Hue / saturation29.2°, 34.0% sat
Price$9.46 / sq ft
Box$165.05 / 17.44 sf (6 pc)
LayoutVertical run, accent walls only

Wood-look ribbed texture, run vertical so the flutes read floor to ceiling. Used behind both bedroom headboards and on the entry accent wall + ceiling — the one warm, textured surface against all the flat checkerboard and glossy wall tile elsewhere.

Against the checkerboard: Zayne's 29° hue is warm, same direction as the checkerboard's own warm undertone — no tension here, unlike the bathroom wall tile story where Lilah's cool teal pulls the other way. At 56% it sits close to Leona's white square (85%) but well clear of the black (16%), so it reads as a mid-value warm accent against the floor's high-contrast pattern.

Summary. Leona and Zayne were never compared against alternatives the way the bathroom wall tile was — both were picked directly and never seriously questioned. They happen to agree in undertone (both warm), which is why the house reads as one consistent palette rather than a room-by-room patchwork.

Bathroom Wall Tile Options

Five wall tile options compared for the three bathrooms — on reflectance, price, format, and how each pairs with the Leona checkerboard floor (white squares ≈85% reflectance, black squares ≈16%, both warm in undertone despite reading as neutral) — the floor the bathrooms were paired with when this comparison was written. Opal color tile is now specified throughout this book — the third pick, after Jaden, Hunter (the original) and Mila, Jade, and cheaper than both. The price and format deltas below are still quoted against Hunter, the original baseline. The bathroom floors have since moved to Dawson, Charcoal (added to the chart below) — the write-ups against each candidate still reflect the original Leona pairing.

Closest match to Hunter's own proportions (same width, just shorter pieces), so the vertical-column look translates most directly. Priciest of the five.

Against the checkerboard: At 43% it clears both extremes (+27 / −42) with the warmest hue of the five (100°). Matte, so it loses Hunter's glossy sheen against the floor — but its 2.5" width means the room's column composition carries over most directly.

Added after spotting it installed: strong piece-to-piece shade variation — pale sage squares scattered among blue-teals — under a wavy high-gloss glaze. The coolest hue on this page (163°, past even Hunter's 134°), leaning teal rather than jade. Cheapest after Dax.

Against the checkerboard: At 49% it sits comfortably between the black and white squares (+33 / −36), nearly as balanced as Mila — but its cool teal hue pulls against the floor's warm undertone, where Mila leans with it.

Mila Jade
4" x 4" · glossy ceramic
CONSIDERED
Reflectance · 54.1%
Hue / saturation92.1°, 16.6% sat
Price$10.38 / sq ft (−20% vs. Hunter)
Box$132.90 / 12.8 sf
Layout impactDifferent scale — small square, not a plank

Lightest of the five options and glossy. Warmer hue than Hunter (92° vs 134°), closer to the floor's own warm undertone.

Against the checkerboard: At 54% it lands almost exactly halfway between the checkerboard's black and white squares (+38 / −31) — a genuine third value, not a near-match to either extreme — and it stays glossy, keeping the glossy-wall/matte-floor sheen contrast.

Summary. Hunter is the darkest option on this page and runs cooler than the checkerboard floor's warm marbling. Mila is the lightest of the five, keeps a glossy finish, and its warm hue sits closest to the floor's own undertone, though it's a small square rather than a plank. Dax is the least expensive by far but matte and a much larger plank. Ellie keeps Hunter's plank width most closely but is matte and the most expensive per square foot. Lilah, added after it was spotted installed, is nearly as balanced as Mila in value and second-cheapest, but reads teal — the coolest hue of the five, pulling against the floor's warm undertone. Seen installed, it won the spec anyway: the variation is the look, and only Dax costs less. Each carries a different trade-off among reflectance, price, format, and finish.
